targets.authors: Tolman EC, Ritchie BF, Kalish D.
targets.title: Studies in spatial learning. I. Orientation and the short-cut.
targets.evidence_quote: This study replicated with human participants the essential features of the seminal short-cutting experiment by Tolman, Ritchie, and Kalish (1946) [14] with rats.
targets.outcome_quote: In the absence of the beacon, participants in group Ambient tended to make path choices in the test that were adjacent to the location of the path that led away from the central chamber during the training phase. This pattern does not conform to that anticipated by Tolman et al., which assumes path choices in the test that were based on the shortest route to the goal location experienced during training. However, in group Light-Light, a close replication of the arrangement in the study of Tolman et al., path choices tended toward the paths leading to the goal/light.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Close Light-Light replication agrees, Ambient conceptual replication does not. Explicit comparison across conditions settles mixed. Other cited short-cut studies supply context and are not independently re-tested.
